研究背景:A/Goose/Guangdong/1/1996(Gs/Gd)谱系H5高致病性禽流感(HPAI)病毒1996年在中国家鹅中首次发现,之后在家禽和野鸟中反复暴发。其血凝素(HA)基因已分化为0–9 clades及多个亚支。clade 2.3.4于2008年在中国出现,演化为2.3.4.4a–h。clade 2.3.4.4b自2014年起与当地禽流感病毒广泛重配,产生H5N2、H5N5、H5N6、H5N8等。至2021年末,clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1成为全球优势HPAI亚型,在亚洲、欧洲、非洲和北美野鸟和家禽中广泛暴发,并因宿主范围扩大和反复溢出至哺乳动物(包括人)引发公共卫生关注。韩国自2003年首次HPAI H5N1侵入后,反复发生H5Nx(H5N1、H5N8、H5N6)暴发,野鸟在引入和传播中持续起关键作用。2020–2021冬季报告234例野鸟clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI病例,2021–2022为47起,2022–2023为174例,2023–2024为19例,季节间规模和病毒活动差异明显,并出现不同基因型,提示反复引入和野鸟种群内重配。2024–2025季节clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1经野鸟传入韩国,且2025年3月在野生豹猫(Prionailurus bengalensis)中检测到HPAI H5N1,为韩国该野生哺乳动物首次记录的溢出事件,显示宿主范围扩大和对动物及公共卫生的持续威胁。因此,研究人员对2024–2025冬季韩国野鸟和豹猫H5N1病毒进行全基因组测序和比较系统发育分析,以阐明时空扩散路径、进化动态和宿主转换。 研究人员开展:2024年10月14日至2025年3月24日,通过国家HPAI监测项目在野生鸟类中报告43例clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1感染,1例豹猫。研究人员对51株H5N1分离株进行全基因组测序,并开展系统发育和贝叶斯系统发育动力学分析。结论:鉴定出9种基因型Kor24–25A至Kor24–25I;Kor24–25A(n=24)最常见,在鹈形目频繁检出,2024年12月至2025年1月最流行;贝叶斯分析基于HA识别三条最可能引入路线,经京畿、济州和朝鲜半岛南部沿海;野鸭为主要储存宿主;大白鹭更频繁受累,提示季节性物种差异。意义:提供HPAI H5N1系统发育动力学、宿主关联和传播模式见解,强调针对关键禽类宿主和高风险地区加强监测。 关键技术方法(不超过250字):样本来源为2024年10月至2025年3月由韩国国家野生动物疾病控制与预防研究所(NIWDC)开展的全国野动物监测,覆盖92个监测点,收集57,067份粪便和1,007份个体鸟拭子,并被动检查419具尸体;从43起暴发中获得51株病毒,包括2025年3月16日豹猫分离株。关键技术包括:实时逆转录聚合酶链反应(rRT-PCR)筛查M和H5基因;Illumina MiSeq全基因组测序并提交GISAID;MAFFT比对,RAxML最大似然(ML)系统发育,iTOL可视化,PopArt最小生成网络,ggFLU基因型分类,FluMut分子标记筛查;TempEst评估分子钟信号;BEAST/BEAUti贝叶斯连续和离散性状系统发育动力学分析,CIPRES运行,Tracer、LogCombiner、TreeAnnotator、FigTree、EvoLaps、SpreaD3和PACT分析传播路线、宿主转换和状态比例。 研究结果: **Multiple genotypes of 2024–2025 HPAI viruses**:研究人员成功对2024年10月14日至2025年3月24日韩国野生动物中51株H5N1 HPAI病毒测序。ML系统发育显示所有基因片段存在多个遗传簇,bootstrap支持>90:PB2三个、PB1四个、PA三个、HA两个、NP五个、NA两个、M一个、NS一个。多数簇内序列>98%成对核苷酸同一性,但A/Mandarin duck/Korea/24WF743–8P/2025的PB1、A/Wild goose/Korea/24WF894–1P/2025和A/Mandarin duck/Korea/24WF266–5P/2024的NS例外。鉴定九种基因型:Kor24–25A(AAAAAAAA;n=24)、Kor24–25B(BBBBBBAB;n=11)、Kor24–25C(AAABAAAA;n=8)、Kor24–25D(AAAADAAA;n=1)、Kor24–25E(ACAACAAA;n=2)、Kor24–25F(CCCACAAA;n=2)、Kor24–25G(AAAAEAAA;n=1)、Kor24–25H(ADAAAAAA;n=1)、Kor24–25I(DAAAAAAA;n=1)。最小生成网络显示病毒大体按基因型聚类,但核苷酸替换数不总严格对应基因型边界。Kor24–25A、B、C为主要基因型;C的HA与B近,其余七片段与A近;其他六种为短暂次要变异,各1–2株,多数片段与A共享但内部基因不同。Kor24–25D、G、H的PB1或NP来自东亚既往HPAI谱系;Kor24–25E、F、I的PB2或NP与中亚和东亚低致病性禽流感(LPAI)病毒近;E和F的PB1形成独立簇,bootstrap 100,与欧洲–俄罗斯HPAI病毒同一性97.5–98.0%。ggFLU等分类显示Kor24–25B对应B23.2–1,GenoFLU A3/A5,GenIn2 EA–2020–C;其余40样本ggFLU为B.18,GenIn2和GenoFLU未分配。FluMut发现十种突变组合A–J;Kor24–25A含F、E、C型,B含G、J型,C含H、I型,其他各单一型,F由四种基因型共享。 **Temporal and host distributions of HPAI viruses**:2024年10月至2025年3月,51株病毒周分布显示,2024年10月第三周首次检测时Kor24–25A和B同时出现,2024年11月D、E、C出现。野鸟HPAI病例2024年12月达峰。2024年12月第三周优势基因型从B转为A。A全季持续,B在2024年12月后未记录;次要基因型2024年12月后零星检出。宿主分布中,鹈形目占最高比例,其次雁形目、猛禽(Falconiformes和Accipitriformes)、鸻形目和食肉目。鹈形目中大白鹭最多(n=22),主要关联Kor24–25A。雁形目基因型多样性最高,检出7种。猛禽检出A、B、C、I四种。三种主要基因型跨多种宿主:A和B除食肉目外所有宿主组,C见于雁形目、食肉目和猛禽。 **Spatiotemporal transmission patterns of HPAI viruses**:基于HA的贝叶斯系统发育动力学揭示2024–2025冬季H5N1时空传播。cluster 1首例为2024年10月14日京畿地区捕获鸳鸯,HA来自Kor24–25A,tMRCA为2024年5月6日(95% HPD:2023年12月20日至2024年8月29日)。连续系统地理学提示京畿道为cluster 1在韩国最可能祖先地点,随后向南部扩散,部分再向北,另一些可能传播至日本南部。cluster 2含Kor24–25B和C的HA,分2a(主要B)和2b(主要C),提示独立引入。2a tMRCA为2024年7月7日(95% HPD:2024年3月27日至9月20日);2b为2024年7月27日(95% HPD:2024年3月23日至11月9日);cluster 2整体tMRCA为2024年2月23日(95% HPD:2023年11月11日至2024年7月26日)。2a最可能祖先地点为济州,随后向北并向东西扩散;2b最可能为朝鲜半岛南部沿海,分两路,一路向北至忠清,一路向南至济州,北上病毒后来沿西部沿海向南移动。 **Transmission of HPAI viruses between host species**:基于HA的宿主离散性状分析中,BF>3且PP>0.5为显著,BF>20且PP>0.9为强支持。cluster 1最可能经野鸭引入(BF=5.448,PP=0.708);随后野鸭至鹭(BF=30.831,PP=0.932)和其他野鸟(BF=5.467,PP=0.708);鹭至其他野鸟(BF=23.587,PP=0.913);野鸭至韩国外谱系(BF=43.286,PP=0.951)强支持。cluster 2同样可能经野鸭从韩国外引入(BF=75.497,PP=0.971);野鸭至其他野鸟(BF=89.554,PP=0.997)和鹭(BF=39.928,PP=0.947)强支持;未推断鹭起源传播。祖先离散状态主干比例随时间依次为韩国外、韩国野鸭、韩国鹭、韩国其他。源–汇动态显示两簇转换事件均发生在2024年Q3,从野鸭到鹭和其他物种;cluster 1另有2024年Q4和2025年Q1鹭到其他物种。Markov rewards显示cluster 1野鸭最高,其次鹭和其他;cluster 2野鸭最高,其他次之,鹭最低。 讨论部分总结:研究人员报告2024–2025冬季野鸟中九种新HPAI基因型,提示clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI与共循环HPAI或LPAI频繁重配。内部基因中M和NS遗传多样性最低,NP形成最多单系枝。Kor24–25A、B、C为主要基因型,时间分布不同;A持续整个监测期,B仅早期至2024年12月第五周,约占采样期一半。早期基因型短暂优势此前已有,但与2021–2022和2022–2023冬季随暴发进展基因型多样性下降不同,本季持续遗传多样性。A、B、C在多种野鸟检出,宿主范围广。雁形目基因型多样性最高,符合其主要水鸟储存库角色;鹭至其他野鸟传播提示鹭可作易感宿主和潜在中间宿主参与本地传播。猛禽基因型多样性第二,与既往低或无禽流感病毒流行报道不同,可能因捕食感染水禽。豹猫Kor24–25C零星感染可能因食入感染野鸟。HA贝叶斯分析识别三个病毒簇,表明至少三次独立引入。cluster 1引入地区既往为HPAI侵入高风险区,来自俄罗斯、蒙古、中国风险高于日本;cluster 2引入地区济州和南部与日本引入风险较高,且2024–2025日本H5 HPAI HA分析显示来自cluster 2a的24WC025与同期日本分离株同枝。2a和2b可能经野鸟独立引入不同地区,所有基因序列与既往野鸟病毒近,重配更可能发生在亚洲迁徙野鸟而非家禽。离散性状分析提示季节特异性宿主分布和传播。既往研究认为野鸭在早期引入和国内传播重要,鹅在后续传播贡献较大;但2024–2025鹅源病毒仅5.9%(3/51),可能反映鹅死亡或尸体检测减少;鹭源病毒43.13%(22/51),明显高于既往HPAI暴发。2022–2023有鹤类(hooded cranes和white-naped cranes)大规模暴发,2024–2025未检出HPAI阳性鹤,显示受影响宿主季节差异。研究人员强调需继续多物种监测和野鸟病理生物学研究。野生鸟源病毒分析需谨慎,因监测可能不完全代表野鸟多样性,并偏向体型较大、数量较多或致病性较高物种。 研究结论翻译:总体而言,基于HA基因的贝叶斯系统发育动力学分析刻画了HPAI H5N1病毒进入韩国的多条引入途径、国内基因型特异性传播模式,以及野鸭和大白鹭在病毒传播中的关键作用。韩国多条引入途径和频繁重配事件的观察强调了该地区HPAI流行病学的复杂性。这些发现为HPAI H5N1病毒传播动力学提供了有价值的见解,并强调针对关键禽类宿主和高风险地理区域加强监测项目的重要性。然而,野生鸟源病毒分析应谨慎解释,因为监测可能不能完全代表野生鸟类种群多样性,并可能偏向体型较大、数量较多或表现出较高致病性的物种。未来整合病理生物学、野生鸟类生态学和候鸟迁徙数据的综合方法将进一步促进对野生鸟类中clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI生态学和流行病学的理解,并提高对未来暴发的准备。 论文解读:韩国野生鸟类中新型重配HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b病毒的多重引入与传播(2024–2025)研究背景:A/Goose/Guangdong/1/1996(Gs/Gd)谱系H5高致病性禽流感(HPAI)病毒1996年在中国家鹅中首次发现,之后在家禽和野鸟中反复暴发。其血凝素(HA)基因已分化为0–9 viruses**:2024年10月至2025年3月,51株病毒周分布显示,2024年10月第三周首次检测时Kor24–25A和B同时出现,2024年11月D、E、C出现。野鸟HPAI病例2024年12月达峰。2024年12月第三周优势基因型从B转为A。A全季持续,B在2024年12月后未记录;次要基因型2024年12月后零星检出。宿主分布中,鹈形目占最高比例,其次雁形目、猛禽(Falconiformes和Accipitriformes)、鸻形目和食肉目。鹈形目中大白鹭最多(n=22),主要关联Kor24–25A。雁形目基因型多样性最高,检出7种。猛禽检出A、B、C、I四种。三种主要基因型跨多种宿主:A和B除食肉目外所有宿主组,C见于雁形目、食肉目和猛禽。**Spatiotemporal transmission patterns of HPAI viruses**:基于HA的贝叶斯系统发育动力学揭示2024–2025冬季H5N1时空传播。cluster 1首例为2024年10月14日京畿地区捕获鸳鸯,HA来自Kor24–25A,tMRCA为2024年5月6日(95% HPD:2023年12月20日至2024年8月29日)。连续系统地理学提示京畿道为cluster 1在韩国最可能祖先地点,随后向南部扩散,部分再向北,另一些可能传播至日本南部。cluster 2含Kor24–25B和C的HA,分2a(主要B)和2b(主要C),提示独立引入。2a tMRCA为2024年7月7日(95% HPD:2024年3月27日至9月20日);2b为2024年7月27日(95% HPD:2024年3月23日至11月9日);cluster 2整体tMRCA为2024年2月23日(95% HPD:2023年11月11日至2024年7月26日)。2a最可能祖先地点为济州,随后向北并向东西扩散;2b最可能为朝鲜半岛南部沿海,分两路,一路向北至忠清,一路向南至济州,北上病毒后来沿西部沿海向南移动。**Transmission of HPAI viruses between host species**:基于HA的宿主离散性状分析中,BF>3且PP>0.5为显著,BF>20且PP>0.9为强支持。cluster 1最可能经野鸭引入(BF=5.448,PP=0.708);随后野鸭至鹭(BF=30.831,PP=0.932)和其他野鸟(BF=5.467,PP=0.708);鹭至其他野鸟(BF=23.587,PP=0.913);野鸭至韩国外谱系(BF=43.286,PP=0.951)强支持。cluster 2同样可能经野鸭从韩国外引入(BF=75.497,PP=0.971);野鸭至其他野鸟(BF=89.554,PP=0.997)和鹭(BF=39.928,PP=0.947)强支持;未推断鹭起源传播。祖先离散状态主干比例随时间依次为韩国外、韩国野鸭、韩国鹭、韩国其他。源–汇动态显示两簇转换事件均发生在2024年Q3,从野鸭到鹭和其他物种;cluster 1另有2024年Q4和2025年Q1鹭到其他物种。Markov rewards显示cluster 1野鸭最高,其次鹭和其他;cluster 2野鸭最高,其他次之,鹭最低。讨论部分总结:研究人员报告2024–2025冬季野鸟中九种新HPAI基因型,提示clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI与共循环HPAI或LPAI频繁重配。内部基因中M和NS遗传多样性最低,NP形成最多单系枝。Kor24–25A、B、C为主要基因型,时间分布不同;A持续整个监测期,B仅早期至2024年12月第五周,约占采样期一半。早期基因型短暂优势此前已有,但与2021–2022和2022–2023冬季随暴发进展基因型多样性下降不同,本季持续遗传多样性。A、B、C在多种野鸟检出,宿主范围广。雁形目基因型多样性最高,符合其主要水鸟储存库角色;鹭至其他野鸟传播提示鹭可作易感宿主和潜在中间宿主参与本地传播。猛禽基因型多样性第二,与既往低或无禽流感病毒流行报道不同,可能因捕食感染水禽。豹猫Kor24–25C零星感染可能因食入感染野鸟。HA贝叶斯分析识别三个病毒簇,表明至少三次独立引入。cluster 1引入地区既往为HPAI侵入高风险区,来自俄罗斯、蒙古、中国风险高于日本;cluster 2引入地区济州和南部与日本引入风险较高,且2024–2025日本H5 HPAI HA分析显示来自cluster 2a的24WC025与同期日本分离株同枝。2a和2b可能经野鸟独立引入不同地区,所有基因序列与既往野鸟病毒近,重配更可能发生在亚洲迁徙野鸟而非家禽。离散性状分析提示季节特异性宿主分布和传播。既往研究认为野鸭在早期引入和国内传播重要,鹅在后续传播贡献较大;但2024–2025鹅源病毒仅5.9%(3/51),可能反映鹅死亡或尸体检测减少;鹭源病毒43.13%(22/51),明显高于既往HPAI暴发。2022–2023有鹤类(hooded cranes和white-naped cranes)大规模暴发,2024–2025未检出HPAI阳性鹤,显示受影响宿主季节差异。研究人员强调需继续多物种监测和野鸟病理生物学研究。野生鸟源病毒分析需谨慎,因监测可能不完全代表野鸟多样性,并偏向体型较大、数量较多或致病性较高物种。研究结论翻译:总体而言,基于HA基因的贝叶斯系统发育动力学分析刻画了HPAI H5N1病毒进入韩国的多条引入途径、国内基因型特异性传播模式,以及野鸭和大白鹭在病毒传播中的关键作用。韩国多条引入途径和频繁重配事件的观察强调了该地区HPAI流行病学的复杂性。这些发现为HPAI H5N1病毒传播动力学提供了有价值的见解,并强调针对关键禽类宿主和高风险地理区域加强监测项目的重要性。然而,野生鸟源病毒分析应谨慎解释,因为监测可能不能完全代表野生鸟类种群多样性,并可能偏向体型较大、数量较多或表现出较高致病性的物种。未来整合病理生物学、野生鸟类生态学和候鸟迁徙数据的综合方法将进一步促进对野生鸟类中clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI生态学和流行病学的理解,并提高对未来暴发的准备。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读!

source_language_evidence.time: “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 2024年10月14日至2025年3月24日期间,通过国家高致病性禽流感(highly pathogenic avian influenza,HPAI)监测项目,在野生鸟类中检测到43例clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI A型(H5N1)感染,并在1只豹猫中检测到1例。研究人员对51株分离株进行了全基因组测序,并调查了其系统发育关系。系统发育分析鉴定出9种不同基因型,命名为Kor24–25A至Kor24–25I。最常检出的基因型Kor24–25A(n = 24)在鹈形目(Pelecaniformes)中频繁检出,并在2024年12月至2025年1月间最为流行。使用HA(hemagglutinin,血凝素)基因序列进行的贝叶斯连续和离散性状系统发育动力学分析(Bayesian continuous and discrete trait phylodynamic analyses)确定了经由京畿道、济州岛和朝鲜半岛南部沿海地区的3条最可能病毒引入途径,并提示野鸭是促进病毒在野生鸟类种群中传播的主要储存宿主。2024–2025季节期间,大白鹭(Ardea alba)似乎比其他野生鸟种更频繁受累,提示野生鸟类中物种特异性疾病结局可能存在季节性差异。该研究为HPAI H5N1病毒的系统发育动力学、宿主关联和传播模式提供了重要见解。它强调针对关键禽类宿主和高风险地理区域的强化监测项目的重要性。

source_language_evidence.brief_en: 韩国野生鸟类中新型重配高致病性禽流感A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b病毒的多重引入、基因型多样性及贝叶斯系统发育动力学(2024–2025) 《Veterinary Research》:Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月09日 来源:Veterinary Research 3.8 编辑推荐: 2024年10月14日至2025年3月24日期间,通过国家高致病性禽流感(highly pathogenic avian influenza,HPAI)监测项目,在野生鸟类中检测到43例clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI A型(H5N1)感染,并在1只豹猫 欢迎领域“高通量小分子筛选解决方案”>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 2024年10月14日至2025年3月24日期间,通过国家高致病性禽流感(highly pathogenic avian influenza,HPAI)监测项目,在野生鸟类中检测到43例clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI A型(H5N1)感染,并在1只豹猫中检测到1例。研究人员对51株分离株进行了全基因组测序,并调查了其系统发育关系。系统发育分析鉴定出9种不同基因型,命名为Kor24–25A至Kor24–25I。最常检出的基因型Kor24–25A(n = 24)在鹈形目(Pelecaniformes)中频繁检出,并在2024年12月至2025年1月间最为流行。使用HA(hemagglutinin,血凝素)基因序列进行的贝叶斯连续和离散性状系统发育动力学分析(Bayesian continuous and discrete trait phylodynamic analyses)确定了经由京畿道、济州岛和朝鲜半岛南部沿海地区的3条最可能病毒引入途径,并提示野鸭是促进病毒在野生鸟类种群中传播的主要储存宿主。2024–2025季节期间,大白鹭(Ardea alba)似乎比其他野生鸟种更频繁受累,提示野生鸟类中物种特异性疾病结局可能存在季节性差异。该研究为HPAI H5N1病毒的系统发育动力学、宿主关联和传播模式提供了重要见解。它强调针对关键禽类宿主和高风险地理区域的强化监测项目的重要性。 论文解读:韩国野生鸟类中新型重配HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b病毒的多。

READ SUMMARY SUBSCRIBE RECEIVE IN PAPER OTHER EDITIONS Back Animal Health & PathologyMarketTrends Avian influenzaH5n1Poultry import ban 07 Oct 2026 Hong Kong suspends poultry imports from areas in US and UK due to avian influenza Hong Kong has contacted the American and British authorities over the issues and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH. aviNews Asia SAVE IN THE LIBRARY PDF FILE The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of Hong Kong’s Food and Environmental Hygiene Department on October 5 instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products, including poultry eggs, due to outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza in areas in the US and the UK with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong. The areas include Big Stone County and Kandiyohi County of the State of Minnesota, Ravalli County of the State of Montana, and Barron County of the State of Wisconsin in the US, and in the Isle of Lewis of Scotland in the UK, according to notifications from the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH). A CFS spokesman said that according to the Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong imported about 24,190 tons of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 20.2 million poultry eggs from the US, and about 340 tons of chilled and frozen poultry meat from the UK in the first six months of this year. “The CFS has contacted the American and British authorities over the issues and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreaks. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation,” the spokesman said. analysis.time: Hong Kong suspended poultry imports from the US and UK on October 5, 2026, with the decision taking effect immediately. The publication date of the news report is October 7, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Hong Kong, specifically the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) under the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, implemented the import ban. The affected population includes individuals who may be exposed to poultry products from the US and UK.
analysis.event: Hong Kong suspended poultry imports from specific areas in the US and UK due to outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza. This action was reported by aviNews.com and confirmed by the CFS.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The import suspension affects poultry meat and products, including eggs, from the US and UK. The CFS cited the import of about 24,190 tons of poultry meat and 20.2 million eggs from the US, and 340 tons of poultry meat from the UK in the first six months of the year. The risk is explicitly stated as being to public health in Hong Kong.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Hong Kong has contacted the American and British authorities regarding the avian influenza outbreaks and will monitor updates from the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and relevant authorities. Appropriate actions will be taken based on the situation's development.

analysis.brief_en: Hong Kong suspended poultry imports from specific areas in the US and UK on October 5, 2026, due to outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza. The decision, effective immediately, aims to protect public health in Hong Kong. The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department issued the directive, citing the import of about 24,190 tons of poultry meat and 20.2 million eggs from the US, and 340 tons of poultry meat from the UK in the first half of 2026. Hong Kong has contacted US and UK authorities and will monitor updates from the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and relevant agencies. The CFS stated that appropriate actions will be taken based on the situation's development. This measure is part of Hong Kong's response to the avian influenza outbreak, which is a primary candidate for analysis under the avian influenza topic contract.
analysis.summary_en: Hong Kong suspended poultry imports from specific areas in the US and UK on October 5, 2026, due to outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza. The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department issued the directive, citing the import of about 24,190 tons of poultry meat and 20.2 million eggs from the US, and 340 tons of poultry meat from the UK in the first half of 2026. Hong Kong has contacted US and UK authorities and will monitor updates from the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and relevant agencies. The CFS stated that appropriate actions will be taken based on the situation's development. elements_zh.time: 香港于2026年10月5日暂停从美国和英国进口家禽,该决定立即生效。该新闻报道发布日期为2026年10月7日。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 香港特别是食物环境卫生署辖下的食物安全中心(中心)实施了进口禁令。受影响的人群包括可能接触来自美国和英国的家禽产品的个人。

The decision, effective immediately, aims to protect public health in Hong Kong. The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department issued the directive, citing the import of about 24,190 tons of poultry meat and 20.2 million eggs from the US, and 340 tons of poultry meat from the UK in the first half of 2026. Hong Kong has contacted US and UK authorities and will monitor updates from the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and relevant agencies. The CFS stated that appropriate actions will be taken based on the situation's development. This measure is part of Hong Kong's response to the avian influenza outbreak, which is a primary candidate for analysis under the avian influenza topic contract.

news.content_title: Ireland enters higher-risk period as winter and migrating birds raise fears of fresh avian influenza cases
news.content: IRELAND is entering a high-risk period for avian influenza as cold weather and migrating birds increase the threat of the disease reaching the country. The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) has confirmed that no wild birds have tested positive for avian influenza in Ireland in recent months. Ireland is now entering a high-risk period for bird flu Credit: DHUB_Search_Alamy_NUK This is due to cold weather and migrating birds increasing the threat of the disease Credit: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire Just two cases of the disease have been recorded in Ireland so far this year. DAFM said the combination of winter conditions and bird migration patterns means the coming months represent a higher-risk period for avian influenza entering Ireland. Sign up to The Irish Sun’s daily newsletter Thank you! A spokesperson said: “As the winter begins to set in, weather conditions and bird migration routes bring a higher risk period for incursion of avian influenza to Ireland. “Colder weather and shorter daylight hours can extend the survival time of avian influenza viruses in the environment, and migratory wild birds (the natural hosts of many avian influenza viruses) arrive in large numbers to overwinter in Ireland.” The department is now urging anyone keeping captive birds to maintain strict biosecurity measures to reduce the risk of infection. DAFM has stressed that strong biosecurity is the most important measure bird owners can take to prevent diseases entering their premises and spreading among poultry. Bird keepers are also being urged to report suspected cases to the authorities through the Department of Agriculture’s Avian Check app or the National Disease Emergency Hotline on 01 492 8026 . The spokesperson added: “All commercial poultry farmers, backyard keepers and those with captive birds should take action to reduce the risk of their flocks becoming infected, for the protection of the Irish poultry industry. Most read in The Irish Sun “Members of the public are advised not to handle sick or dead wild birds they come across.” The warning comes after detections of highly pathogenic avian influenza in birds continued to fall across the EU , following a decline that had already been recorded during the spring. Despite the lower number of cases, the disease remains a threat to poultry producers. This is because outbreaks can lead to restrictions on bird movements and other measures designed to prevent further spread. The EU has recently announced €73million in agricultural reserve funding for Italy to help farmers affected by outbreaks of avian influenza and African swine fever. Of that amount, €61million will be directed towards poultry and egg producers who were impacted by avian influenza outbreaks between September 2022 and March 2025. The funding is intended to help compensate farmers for financial losses caused by measures introduced to contain and prevent the spread of the diseases. France has also faced a major impact from avian influenza, with the country experiencing a major resurgence of highly pathogenic cases during the 2025-2026 epidemiological season. A total of 156 outbreaks were recorded in France during the season, including 125 on commercial poultry farms. Authorities introduced a range of sanitary measures to limit transmission, including restrictions on the movement of poultry within areas subject to disease controls. The measures had financial repercussions throughout the poultry sector, affecting businesses beyond farms where outbreaks were recorded. French Agriculture Minister Annie Genevard has since announced a €10million financial assistance scheme for businesses involved in hatchery operations, collection and downstream activities

The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) has confirmed that no wild birds have tested positive for avian influenza in recent months, but the risk is rising due to colder weather and shorter daylight hours, which can extend the survival time of the virus in the environment. The DAFM is urging bird keepers, including commercial poultry farmers and backyard bird owners, to implement strict biosecurity measures to prevent the disease from entering their premises. Authorities are also encouraging the public to report suspected cases through the Avian Check app or the National Disease Emergency Hotline. While the exact number of cases in Ireland is not specified, the disease remains a threat to the poultry industry, with potential for outbreaks that could lead to restrictions on bird movements. The EU has recently announced €73 million in agricultural reserve funding for Italy to assist farmers affected by avian influenza and African swine fever, highlighting the broader impact of the disease on the agricultural sector.

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 爱尔兰,重点关注家禽生产者,包括商业家禽养殖场、后院饲养员和圈养鸟类的饲养员。
analysis_zh.event: 由于天气寒冷和候鸟迁徙,爱尔兰正进入 禽流感 的高风险期。农业、食品和海洋部 (DAFM) 已确认近几个月没有 野生鸟类 检测呈阳性,但风险正在增加。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该疾病仍然对家禽生产者构成威胁,暴发 有可能导致限制鸟类活动和采取其他措施以防止进一步传播。欧盟已宣布为受影响的农民提供资金,但证据并未量化对爱尔兰的具体影响。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 农业部敦促鸟类饲养者保持严格的生物安全措施,并通过禽类检查应用程序或国家疾病紧急热线报告可疑病例。目前正在积极监测和评估局势。

Experts explain how Alex Megerle 30 Sep 2026 Feature story Despite a drop in deforestation in 2025, forest losses pile up in the Mekong Gerald Flynn 29 Sep 2026 Quickly stay updated with our news shorts Australia’s new eco police flexes muscles with major wildlife trafficking bust Mongabay.com 8 Oct 2026 Australian authorities have disrupted an alleged wildlife trafficking syndicate, uncovering a clandestine operation where smuggled native animals were hoarded alongside caches of cash and gold, reports contributor Johan Augustin for Mongabay. The operation reportedly seized 28 native and a few exotic species alongside approximately A$300,000 (nearly $210,000) in cash, gold, and silver bullion on July 16. The bust marks the first major wildlife crime investigation carried out by the new National Environmental Protection Agency (National EPA), Australia’s first independent federal environmental regulator, launched on July 1. In addition to the 28 native Australian reptiles — including shingleback lizards (Tiliqua rugosa), spiny-tailed skinks (Egernia stokesii), and lace monitors (Varanus varius) — there were heavily regulated nonnative species like a North American hognose snake (genus Heterodon) and a ball python (Python regius). The agency alleges the native species were supplied to foreign nationals for illegal export. “Illegal trade of Australia’s native wildlife is a serious crime,” Dani Yannopoulos, head of the National EPA’s environmental permitting and compliance division, said in a media release published Aug. 22. “Australia’s native wildlife is precious and we are working closely with [Australian] Border Force and international partners to stop those who attempt to exploit it through the illegal wildlife trade.” Yannopoulos added that anyone taking part in the illegal wildlife trade risks serious penalties. Under Australian federal environmental law, exporting native animals or eggs without a permit carries penalties of up to 10 years in prison and fines reaching A$364,000 ($253,000). Even so, immense profits continue to incentivize criminal syndicates. Native lizards that sell legally in Australia for A$100 to A$400 ($70 to $280) can command between A$1,000 and A$20,000 ($700 and $14,000) on foreign black markets. “Wildlife trafficking is worth about $30 billion a year in the East Asia and Pacific region alone,” Tanya Plibersek, Australia’s minister for the environment and water, said in a press release. “The price of Australian reptiles on the international black market can be more than 28 times the domestic price.” Plibersek added that Australian wildlife is highly lucrative to criminals and organized crime syndicates, “especially those animals that are already vulnerable or threatened with extinction.” Between June 2025 and May 2026, authorities intercepted 113 illegal exports involving 1,250 native animals, according to the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water. “Australian reptiles have always been common and attractive in the exotic pet trade,” said Phil Cassey, director at the Wildlife Crime Research Hub. “We’re also seeing a rise in non-native pet species coming ... into Australia, including mammals and most recently a big rise in the popularity of insect and invertebrate species — including spiders, scorpions, cockroaches and ants.” Read the full story by Johan Augustin here. Banner image: In its first major operation since being established on July 1, Australia’s National EPA seized reptiles, including hognose snakes and ball pythons. Image courtesy of the National EPA. Logging threatens Bornean forest earmarked for Indigenous Peace Park Mongabay.com 8 Oct 2026 Part of a forest in Malaysian Borneo that Indigenous communities had envisioned co-managing and self-governing has been turned into an active commercial logging concession, according to a recent civil society report. The 283,500-hectare (700,500-acre) Upper Baram Forest Area, in the northeastern part of the state of Sarawak, was proposed as a community-led conservation area more than 15 years ago. In 2021, the Sarawak Forest Department secured $1.4 million from the International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO), which promotes the sustainable use of forests, to develop a conservation initiative with 32 Indigenous villages, called the Baram Peace Park. However, the state government subsequently granted a 170,000-hectare (420,000-acre) timber concession in 2024 to a company called Borneoland Timber Resources Sdn. Bhd., overlapping key cultural and ecological zones, reports contributor Danielle Keeton-Olsen for Mongabay. According to a report from Swiss-based nonprofit Bruno Manser Fonds, a key funder of the Baram Peace Park project, between March and May 2025, community observers tracked more than 160 logging trucks exiting the concession monthly. These trucks hauled an estimated 10.5 million ringgit ($2.6 million) in timber per month. Logging paths have penetrated core primary forest around Gunung Murud Kecil, a peak central to the Indigenous Penan heritage, threatening protected species including helmeted hornbills (Rhinoplax vigil), sun bears (Helarctos malayanus), and Sunda clouded leopards (Neofelis diardi). Affected villagers allege loggers have violated native customary rights by bulldozing land and destroying ancestral fruit trees. Komeok Joe, CEO and founder of the Penan rights organization Keruan, said local communities are actively monitoring and mobilizing to defend their forests. “If the logging doesn’t stop this year, the forest might be finished in those two areas,” he said. State authorities, however, defend the timber concession. Hamden Mohammad, director of the Sarawak Forest Department, told Mongabay that Bruno Manser Fonds held a “misunderstanding — or misrepresentation — of the project’s original concept and objectives.” He added the project was always intended as an “integrated landscape management area” that permitted timber licensing alongside community use and conservation. Mohammad also pointed to a decision by the High Court of Sabah and Sarawak, dismissing an Indigenous-led challenge, as an indication that there were no irregularities with the timber concession. “Accordingly, assertions that the concession was improperly granted solely because it was not subject to a public tender process are not supported by the relevant legal requirements or the Court’s findings,” he said. Mohammad added that not all communities in Upper Baram are opposed to Borneoland’s logging activities. However, he acknowledged the recent blockades held by some residents were a sign that Indigenous communities were frustrated with the concession. Read the full story by Danielle Keeton-Olsen here. Banner image: Timber is chopped and tagged for transport at a logging area near the site of the former Baram dam blockade on Aug. 22, 2023. Image by Danielle Keeton-Olsen for Mongabay. Despite legacy court case, Zambian Vedanta mine pollution continues Victoria Schneider 8 Oct 2026 The Zambian government is investigating a chemical spill in its Copperbelt Province allegedly linked to Konkola Copper Mines (KCM), owned by U.K.-based multinational Vedanta Resources. Residents in Chingola district told Mongabay they observed discoloration of the Kafue River and fish die-off on Sept. 28, raising fresh concerns about the environmental and social impacts of mining operations in one of Zambia’s most important copper-producing regions. According to a statement by Gilbert Siame, Zambia’s minister of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), the incident was caused by a leaking pipe at KCM’s tailings leach plant and an overflow from the company’s pollution control dam outside Chingola. “The pollution control dam was full, that’s why it spilled,” Eugene Mulenga, Chingola-based human rights activist and coordinator for caritas, told Mongabay. “The [chemical] discharge happens all the time, mostly at night, and the local residents consume this water because they don’t have another option.” Following the Sept. 28 spill, tests conducted by the Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA), KCM and local water utility Mulonga Water Supply and Sanitation Company showed elevated levels of turbidity and conductivity downstream along the Kafue River. In a statement issued Oct. 1, KCM contested its responsibility in the spillage, saying that company officials reported the incident to ZEMA and asked for a fact-based investigation. Mongabay reached out to the company but did not receive a response by the time of publication. Siame noted in the statement shared with Mongabay that authorities are still testing water samples to confirm heavy metals and other contaminants. He added the ministry has ordered KCM to conduct a comprehensive assessment of its pollution control dams, tailings pipelines and related infrastructure to determine whether other facilities could pose environmental risks. “The Ministry is consulting with relevant stakeholders on the appropriate penal sanctions against the polluter in accordance with the provisions of the Environmental Management Act,” he wrote in the statement. Under this law, major toxic discharges or hazardous waste violations can result in penalties of up to 280,000 Kwacha ($14,000). The Sept. 28 incident adds to a long history of environmental concerns surrounding KCM and other mining companies operating in Zambia’s Copperbelt. KCM was previously at the center of a major legal case in the U.K. following a 2008 pollution incident. The case was settled out of court in 2021, with the company paying compensation to around 2,500 affected villagers “without admission of liability.” KCM, one of Zambia’s largest copper producers, is expanding and recapitalizing mining and processing operations in the country as the government seeks to more than triple national copper output in the coming years. Vedanta Resources owns 80% stake in KCM. The Zambian government had placed KCM into liquidation in 2019, citing concerns including tax evasion, unpaid debts, inadequate investment and environmental pollution, but the company picked up operations again in 2024. Banner image: Dead fish at Hippo Pool, north of Chingola, where the Kafue River narrows into a shallow valley. Image by Victoria Schneider for Mongabay. Africa’s monitored wildlife populations declined 80% since 1970, new report says David Akana 7 Oct 2026 Africa’s monitored wildlife populations have declined an average of 80% since 1970, according to a new global assessment. The report also points to pockets of recovery where conservation efforts have been maintained over decades. The report on the decline in the average size of monitored populations was released Oct. 8 in the Living Planet Report 2026. It tracked monitored populations of mammals, birds, fish, reptiles and amphibians between 1970 and 2022. Africa’s 80% decline compares with a global average of 73%; Latin America and the Caribbean recorded the largest regional decline, at 95%. The findings come as governments prepare to assess progress on the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, whose 23 targets include commitments to halt human-induced extinctions and support the recovery of threatened species by 2030. The framework also calls for conserving at least 30% of the world’s land, inland waters and seas by 2030. The Living Planet Index, managed by the Zoological Society of London in partnership with the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), draws on 35,803 population trends from 5,790 vertebrate species worldwide. The index measure changes in the average size of monitored populations, it does not mean that Africa lost 80% of its wild animals or wildlife species, a press release obtained by Mongabay cautions. Habitat destruction and degradation are the most frequently reported pressures on the wildlife populations tracked globally, the report finds. Overexploitation, climate change, pollution, disease and invasive species are among the other threats identified. In the Congo Basin, for example, those pressures include expanding agriculture, logging and mining, as well as roads and other infrastructure that fragment forests and make previously remote areas more accessible, according to the report. Hunting and poaching add to the pressure. WWF says African forest elephant (Loxodonta cyclotis) populations have fallen by more than 60% over recent decades, largely because of habitat loss and illegal killing for ivory. “Reversing this trend requires coordinated action across governments, civil society and other sectors, with Indigenous Peoples and local communities at the centre,” said Nadège Nzoyem, WWF’s regional director for the Congo Basin, in the release. The global numbers show that conservation can make a difference. Half the populations included in the index are either stable or increasing but steep declines among the remaining populations are large enough to pull the overall index sharply downward. As an example, in Southern Africa savanna elephants (Loxodonta africana) remain endangered and are declining across much of their range, the report reveals. But some populations are increasing in places where communities help directly manage wildlife and benefit from doing so. Those efforts have been accompanied by anti-trafficking measures, judicial reforms and efforts to reduce corruption. The report argues protecting individual species and habitats will not be enough. Food and energy production as well as financial systems are underlying forces that must also change to reverse biodiversity decline, the report notes. Banner image: Namibian elephants in Etosha. Image courtesy of Stephan Scholvin. supplementary_news.content: The sweeter side of veterinary medicine Welcome to your new favorite place to grow in vet med. Discover brilliant experts, engaging videos, interactive quizzes, inspiring stories, and podcasts that keep you curious, connected, and excited about what's next. From seahorses to kangaroos, Dr. Olivia Clarke has spent her career proving that birds and exotics deserve the same gold-standard care as any dog or cat, and that leaving full-time clinical work does not make you any less of a veterinarian. New research shows Staph aureus uses milk lipids to triple its envelope thickness and boost pigment, increasing antibiotic tolerance in mastitis. A Seoul National University pilot study found the non-opioid analgesic opiranserin reduced intraoperative rescue analgesia in dogs undergoing castration. Have experience with horses? Take a 5–10 minute survey for a veterinary thesis on equine asthma and how climate and environment affect respiratory symptoms. Montana Tech's Dr. Amy Kuenzi has tracked hantavirus in deer mice for nearly 30 years. Now her team is finding Bartonella in Montana rodents for the first time. A USDA and University of Minnesota model shows dead-bird sampling beats live-bird testing for detecting avian influenza in vaccinated flocks. A bat that touched a child in Yuba City, California, tested positive for rabies. Key reminders for veterinary teams on bat exposures and pet vaccination. Chewy Health is now accepting nominations for the 2027 Chewy Veterinary Leaders Program. The program recognizes second-year veterinary students from backgrounds with limited access to veterinary careers and who have shown an interest in developing their leadership skills. Shelters and clinics in East Idaho report a surge in feline panleukopenia. What veterinarians need to know about diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. 11 careers. 6 questions. Zero chill. Veterinary medicine isn't one job—it's about eleven careers hiding under the same white coat. There is a conversation happening in break rooms, group chats, and parking lots all over veterinary medicine. It usually starts the same way. I love the medicine, but I do not know how much longer I can do this. And it usually ends with a quiet assumption that something is wrong with the person saying it. Somewhere along the way, veterinary medicine developed an unwritten rule: clinical practice is the real job, and everything else is quitting. It gets absorbed in school, reinforced in practice, and carried around as guilt by veterinarians who are exhausted, curious, or simply ready for a change but afraid that stepping out of the exam room means abandoning their oath. If you are graduating this year, the offers are probably already arriving, and some of the numbers are eye-watering. Signing bonuses have become the headline of new grad recruitment, and with student debt where it is, nobody could blame you for reading the biggest number and reaching for a pen. Vet school can turn almost anything into a performance metric. Grades, class rank, clinical skills, productivity, sleep, exercise, and sometimes even food can quietly become one more thing you feel like you should be “doing right.” Add long days, irregular schedules, stress, limited money, constant comparison, and a culture that can reward pushing through discomfort, and it is easy for a complicated relationship with food or your body to hide in plain sight. There are queer and trans veterinarians who came before you, students at other schools experiencing many of the same things, peer-support volunteers willing to listen, community organizations that know your city, and national groups that can help when a problem becomes medical, legal, academic, or overwhelming. Vet school has a way of eating your entire calendar. Between exams, labs, rotations, boards, jobs, relationships, and trying to get enough sleep to remain functional, personal health can slide down the priority list pretty quickly. There is a particular kind of kitchen alchemy that happens when nothing gets thrown away: a roast chicken becomes dinner, then lunch, then the broth for Thursday's ramen. A single Sunday afternoon becomes a month of breakfasts. What follows is not a diet plan so much as a system, one built on a $500 monthly grocery budget, a single person's appetite, and the stubborn belief that homemade is both cheaper and better. McPaul Hermoso started veterinary school at 35 after earning multiple degrees and living in five countries. Discover his unconventional journey, lifelong dream of becoming a veterinarian, and mission to inspire others. From four years cheering at LSU to studying veterinary medicine at the Royal Veterinary College, Jalyne Blackwell is building a career by saying yes to the opportunities that scare her a little—and trusting that the unexpected path might be the right one. After France’s competitive exams shut the door, this 20-year-old found her calling 800 miles from home — and proof that a detour can still lead exactly where you were meant to go. Meet Taja Bell, an LSU veterinary student, Army Animal Care Specialist, mom and model working toward a future in emergency medicine and surgery. There is a particular kind of courage it takes to walk away from a career you have already proven yourself in and start over as a first-year student. Emese Avdeyenkova has done exactly that, twice over, once when she traded a biology degree for an Army uniform, and again when she traded that uniform for a white coat. Now she is bringing all of it, the discipline, the humility, and the hard-won perspective, to Vet Candy Radio as one of the vet student hosts of Vet School After Dark. The former UC Davis Division I athlete turned WesternU veterinary student is bringing the lessons she learned on the court into veterinary medicine—and she already has her sights set on practice ownership. From a shelter medicine internship to the microphone of Vet Candy's new student-led podcast, Jess Mitchell is building a career around one big idea: more pets deserve to stay in the homes that love them. America's favorite vet receptionist Caitlin Palmer and her cat daddy husband Clay Palmer dig into the real science, history, and psychology behind humanity's longest-running obsession. We're talking ancient Egypt, where cats were literally worshipped as gods. We're talking the internet, where cats generate more content than almost anything else on the planet. From ancient worship to TikTok stardom, cats have clawed their way into our hearts and honestly, they never asked for permission. But why? What is it about the most indifferent creature on the planet that makes humans absolutely lose their minds? Think black cats bring bad luck? Think again. The truth about black cats is stranger, richer, and way more interesting than the superstition and Caitlin and Clay are here to set the record straight. In this episode of Cat Cafe, America's favorite vet receptionist Caitlin Palmer and her cat daddy husband Clay Palmer dive deep into the wild world of cat mythology, feline folklore, and the weirdest cat superstitions that humans have carried for centuries. We are talking black cats across cultures — feared in some, worshipped in others. We are talking mythological cats from ancient Egypt to Norse legends to the shadowy corners of the internet. We are talking the real history behind the myths that still follow these animals into shelters today, where black cats consistently wait the longest for homes. Spoiler: the cats were never the problem. Think you know everything about cats? In this hilarious episode of Cat Cafe, America's favorite vet receptionist Caitlin Palmer takes on the ultimate cat trivia challenge — and her cat daddy husband Clay is putting her knowledge to the test. From quirky cat facts to surprising feline science, this quiz will challenge even the most devoted cat lovers. Play along and see if you can beat America’s favorite veterinary receptionist, Caitlin Palmer! But it's not just fun and games. Every wrong answer comes with a punishment — and that punishment is pickle juice. Yes, really. Watch to find out who walks away victorious and who walks away regretting their cat knowledge gaps. • Fun (and tricky) cat trivia questions • Surprising cat facts you probably didn’t know • A very questionable pickle juice challenge Who’s the ultimate cat nerd... and who’s about to drink pickle juice? In this hilarious episode of Pet Candy, Caitlin and Clay go head-to-head in a cat trivia challenge with a twist—get a question wrong, and you have to take a sip of pickle juice Think you know cats? Play along and see if you can beat them (without the punishment.) Every NAVLE Warrior asks some version of the same question during week six: am I studying the right way, or am I just studying the most? Cognitive science has a real answer to that question, and it is not the one most students expect Every NAVLE study plan is built around content: which species, which systems, which diagnoses to drill. But the brain that has to hold all of that information is a physical organ, and it runs on three inputs: sleep, movement, and nutrition. Neglect any one of them and the same number of practice questions will produce worse results. Here's the science behind why, and what to actually do about it. Starting with the October to November 2026 testing window, the NAVLE looks different in two ways that actually matter for how you study. The exam moved to a new block format back in the spring update, and now the ICVA has also refreshed the Species and Diagnosis list itself, adding more than 100 diseases across the species you'll be tested on. That is not a small revision. That is the blueprint growing, and it means the way you have been prepping needs a second look. Paid NAVLE prep services can cost more than $600 for a thirty month pass, sometimes more. For companies selling them, that is a subscription. For a fourth-year veterinary student, that can be groceries for two months. And in a year when gas prices and food prices have squeezed every budget in America, plenty of vet students are doing math far scarier than anything on the exam. There are continuing education programs, and then there are continuing education programs where you accidentally debunk a mythical creature between bites of fried dough. This particular offering from Vet Candy lands firmly in the second category. Based on a short story by Vet Candy’s CEO and X-Files super fan, Dr. Jill Lopez. Dr. Joya Griffin and Dr. Forrest Cummings just dropped the veterinary CE series that changes how you think about complex cases and it is free with your Vet Candy membership. Free RACE-approved veterinary CE is now available on Vet Candy with Unleash Your Inner Hero! , an 8-module urgent care program led by veterinary criticalist Dr. Natosha Richardson. Offering 3.5 RACE CE credits for veterinarians and veterinary technicians, this course covers triage, CPR, supportive care, diagnostics, and treatment across neurologic, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and integumentary emergencies. Free RACE-approved veterinary CE is now available on Vet Candy with Dermatology Secrets featuring Dr. Joya Griffin. This three-part online course is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians and covers the dermatology skills that matter most in everyday practice — skin cytology, histopathology and biopsy interpretation, and the strangest and most diagnostically challenging cases in specialist dermatology. Learn how to read a cytology slide with confidence, decode a dermatopathology report, and work through complex skin presentations that have not responded to standard treatment. Earn 1.5 RACE CE credits at no cost with your free Vet Candy Membership! Free RACE-approved veterinary CE is now available on Vet Candy with the Respiratory Disease Master Course featuring Criticalist Dr. Anthony Gonzalez. Brought to you by Trudell Animal Health, this 8-module course provides 4 RACE CE credits for veterinarians and veterinary technicians. It covers recognition, diagnosis, and management of acute and chronic respiratory disease, including practical guidance on critical care, advanced monitoring, oxygen therapy, and evidence-based treatment strategies. Designed for immediate clinical application, this course helps veterinary professionals improve outcomes in high-stakes respiratory cases. Free RACE-approved veterinary CE is now available on Vet Candy with Endocrinology Secrets featuring Dr. Forrest Cummings. This online course is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians and covers real-world management of diabetes in dogs and cats, Cushing’s disease, and Addison’s disease. Learn how to interpret diagnostics, manage challenging endocrine cases, and improve patient outcomes with practical, case-based guidance. Earn 2 RACE CE credits at no cost—no subscription or credit card required. The Gut-Brain connection is more connected than we thought. This episode of Catching Up explores the fascinating link between the gut and brain in pets. Could your patient's GI issues be tied to behavior? The science says yes. Acute Kidney Injury Alert: New Biomarkers That Could Save Lives. Dr. Elan Armstrong & Dr. Shannon Gregoire break down the newest research on acute kidney injury. World-First Breakthrough: Stem Cells from Cats Could Revolutionize Kidney Disease Treatment! Vet Candy has the details with Dr. Elan & Dr. Shannon. Big news in hemangiosarcoma research! Tune in as we cover a promising breakthrough that could change the way we approach this aggressive cancer. Inside: Dr. Wailani Sung helps you learn how to Recognize the Subtle Signs of Pain in Cats. Presented by Zoetis, maker of Solensia. SolensiaVetTeam.com A cat eye that won't heal is one of those cases that can quietly spiral into something serious — fast. In this episode of Rounds with Dr. Shannon, Dr. Shannon Gregoire sits down with veterinary ophthalmologist Dr. DJ Haeussler for a real clinical conversation about the feline eye cases that challenge general practitioners the most, starting with the corneal ulcer that just won't close. A limping dog walks into your exam room. The owner says it started two weeks ago. The leg looks fine. The X-rays look fine. Nothing adds up — yet. In this episode of Mystery Case Rounds, Dr. Shannon Gregoire walks through a real clinical case of canine lameness from the first exam to the final diagnosis, showing exactly how she thinks through a case when the answer isn't obvious. Veterinary emergency specialist Dr. Kristin Welch walks through a real hyperglycemia case that didn't follow the textbook. Watch the diagnostic reasoning unfold on Vet Candy's Mystery Case Rounds. Dr. Ashley Bourgeois breaks down what is really going on when a Pomeranian loses its coat, the hormonal, genetic, and inflammatory factors may be at play, why this breed is uniquely predisposed to certain dermatologic conditions, and how to build a workup that actually leads somewhere instead of chasing your tail. Nearly a quarter of homeless youth in the U.S. have pets — and some choose veterinary care over their own health care. The Seattle One Health Clinic offers both, side by side, for free. Jeremiah Pouncy shares why this One Health model is changing how we think about the human-animal bond and community care. In Barcelona, scientists are building a biological deep freeze for endangered species, storing genetic material from nearly 300 species and using AI to unlock the future of conservation. Jeremiah Pouncy explains how the Barcelona CryoZoo could change everything we know about saving wildlife from extinction. With fewer than 800 left on Earth, the Bengal florican is one of the rarest birds alive. But in India's Manas National Park, over 800 former poachers have become the species' fiercest protectors. Jeremiah Pouncy tells the remarkable story of how community-led conservation turned a near-extinction into a comeback. A new study on the "Capitoline dolphins" off Rome's coast reveals a population in crisis. Seven out of ten show signs of malnutrition, many bear scars from fishing gear, and scientists warn they may disappear without urgent intervention. Jeremiah Pouncy breaks down what is threatening one of the world's most historically significant dolphin populations and why it matters. Going back to veterinary school usually means new classes, new rotations, new schedules, and the familiar feeling that summer disappeared way too fast. For the hosts of Vet School After Dark , it also means catching up on where everyone spent the break and figuring out how to mentally transition back into another demanding academic year. Vet Candy's hit podcast recently went live in Nashville, and what started as another fast-paced battle of veterinary knowledge quickly turned into something no one in the room saw coming. Dr. Lauren Downey Koos didn't have to look far to get to WVC Nashville. She works at BluePearl Veterinary in Franklin, Tennessee, which means the conference is essentially in her backyard. She graduated from the University of Florida in 2018, went into neurology, and became a specialist faster than most people finish paying off their student loans. Hosts Caitlin and Clay Palmer, the masterminds behind Vet Candy's trivia and news game show, challenge Carey to a fast-paced reckoning with the week's wildest veterinary headlines, most surprising research breakthroughs, and oddest animal stories circulating through the profession. It's loosely inspired by NPR's Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me, except everyone involved actually knows what a splenectomy is. Veterinary technicians Peter Carlos and Jaycee join Vet Candy's Medical Mysteries to tell the story of a cat with an acutely enlarged abdomen and a diagnosis nobody saw coming. Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google Add on Google Not now 10/08/2026 - 12:40 PM Second-generation oral mucosal vaccine candidate (VXA-H5-02) induced robust cross-neutralizing antibodies, significantly reduced viral load, and completely protected against lethal clade 2.3.4.4b viral challenge SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vaxart, Inc. (OTCQX: VXRT), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing oral recombinant vaccines administered via tablet, today announced the publication of positive preclinical study results evaluating its adenovirus-based oral mucosal vaccine platform against Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1, a pathogenic virus that poses a significant threat to public health. The complete, peer-reviewed study results, which were published in Frontiers in Immunology, demonstrate that Vaxart’s second-generation vaccine candidate, VXA-H5-02, elicits both mucosal and systemic neutralizing antibody responses, offering comprehensive protection against lethal challenge with H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b. The company previously reported topline study results in 2025. "The potential spread of H5N1 avian influenza across livestock and mammals underlines the critical need for scalable, rapidly deployable vaccines," said Dr. Sean Tucker, CSO of Vaxart. "These data further support our oral mucosal vaccination technology and highlight the improved immune-stimulating activity of our second-generation H5 construct. The 100% survival rate following challenge with a lethal dose of virus underscores the robust immune protection our oral influenza vaccine candidates may be able to provide. This protection, combined with ease of self-administration and the elimination of complex cold-chain requirements required for injected vaccines, supports the potential of our platform in enabling a novel approach to influenza prevention and pandemic preparedness.” Key Study Highlights 100% Survival Rate: All ferrets immunized with VXA-H5-02 survived a lethal challenge with H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, whereas 100% of unvaccinated control animals rapidly succumbed to infection by Day 6 post-challenge (p< 0.001). Significant Viral Load & Shedding Reduction: VXA-H5-02 vaccination produced a ~2.3-log reduction in infectious viral shedding by Day 3 post-challenge compared to controls. By Day 6–7, viable virus was below the limit of detection in nasal wash samples, and 7 out of 8 animals completely cleared viral RNA by Day 8/9. Mucosal & Cross-Neutralizing Immunity: Immunization with VXA-H5-02 elicited strong serum neutralizing titers and mucosal IgA/IgG responses in nasal wash fluid. Higher pre-challenge nasal IgA levels showed the strongest negative correlation with post-challenge viral shedding (r = -0.6059). Cross-Clade Protection: Serum from VXA-H5-02 immunized animals demonstrated cross-neutralizing activity against divergent H5 strains, including the recently emerged H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1e. Additionally, the clade-mismatched first-generation vaccine (ND1.1, encoding clade 2.1.3.2) conferred 37% survival against the clade 2.3.4.4b challenge. About the Study In the study, non-replicating recombinant adenovirus type 5 (rAd5) vectors expressing viral hemagglutinin (HA) were administered directly to the small intestine of ferrets via endoscopic delivery on Day 0 and Day 28. Ferrets cannot use human tablets, so a liquid formulation delivery method was used to simulate enteric-coated tablet release. On Day 56, animals were challenged intranasally with 1 x 105 TCID50 H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b virus. Protective efficacy, clinical symptoms, mucosal/systemic antibody titers, and viral shedding (measured by RT-qPCR and TCID50) were systematically monitored. About Vaxart Vaxart is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a range of oral recombinant vaccines based on its proprietary delivery platform. Vaxart vaccines are designed to be administered using pills that can be stored and shipped without refrigeration and eliminate the risk of needle-stick injury. Vaxart believes that its proprietary pill vaccine delivery platform is suitable to deliver recombinant vaccines, positioning the Company to develop oral versions of currently marketed vaccines and to design recombinant vaccines for new indications. Vaxart’s development programs currently include pill vaccines designed to protect against coronavirus, norovirus, and influenza, as well as a therapeutic vaccine for human papillomavirus (HPV), Vaxart’s first immune-oncology indication. Vaxart has filed broad domestic and international patent applications covering its proprietary technology and creations for oral vaccination using adenovirus and TLR3 agonists. supplementary_news.content: RACINE COUNTY, Wis. — A case of avian influenza was identified in a poultry flock in Racine County, according to the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection. DATCP said the birds in the backyard poultry flock have been depopulated and won’t enter the food system. The highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as bird flu, is highly contagious. It’s caused by influenza type A viruses. While HPAI can fluctuate in severity, it is often deadly to domestic poultry. It can spread when coming into contact with an infected bird, being around wild birds or being in contact with bird droppings, clothing worn by someone working with animals or equipment used with animals. The bird flu has been moving throughout the U.S. since Dec. 2021. Aly Prouty - Digital Media Producer Aly Prouty is a digital producer for Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin, Ohio and Kentucky. An award-winning, multimedia journalist, she holds an honors B.A. in journalism from Marquette University and an M.A. in journalism and media studies from The University of Alabama

supplementary_news.content: default-output-block.skip-main News & Analysis on the Dairy Industry & Markets Sign inRegister Search menu home menu home NewsSectorsTrendsBig brandsResourcesEvents Close menuQueryly search Home NewsShow News sub sections Industry voices Ingredients Innovation & NPD Manufacturers Markets Mergers & acquisitions Processing & packaging R&D Regulation & safety Retail & shopper insights Partner Feature SectorsShow Sectors sub sections Butter & spreads Cheese Dairy alternatives Dairy beverages Fresh milk Ice cream Yogurt & desserts TrendsShow Trends sub sections Clean label Emerging markets Functional dairy Organic & high welfare farming Reformulation Smart packaging Sustainability Technology & science Big brandsShow Big brands sub sections Arla Foods Danone Fonterra FrieslandCampina Lactalis Nestlé Unilever Yili ResourcesShow Resources sub sections Ingredients Processing equipment & systems, automation, control Packaging & packing materials, containers Filling & packaging equipment & systems Partners EventsShow Events sub sections Shows & conferences Spotlight on Online events Editorial webinars Awards Partner Webinars CONTINUE TO SITE Or wait...11s Renewed call for raw dairy ban amid H5N1 concerns By Michelle Perrett 06-Oct-2026 Last updated on 06-Oct-2026 at 09:30 GMT AAP renews call for raw dairy ban amid H5N1 concerns. (Getty Images) Unpasteurised milk, cheese and other raw dairy products are unsafe to consume and may be linked to the spread of avian influenza, updated guidance from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has said. The AAP said raw dairy products pose the greatest risk to young children and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding. The organisation has renewed its call for a ban on the sale and distribution of raw milk and dairy products, including raw cheeses, citing the increased risk of life-threatening infections. It added that claims that raw milk provides superior health benefits are not supported by scientific evidence. Despite these concerns, the sale and distribution of raw milk products remain legal in at least 27 states across the USA. Raw milk is milk obtained from cows, goats or sheep that has not undergone pasteurization, the process of heating milk to eliminate harmful bacteria and other pathogens. Recommended for you Story continues below... Studies link dairy cow personality traits to milk yields Supply chain pressures are testing dairy’s resilience The protein glut is challenging dairy’s tight milk pool The policy statement from AAP called “Consumption of Unpasteurized (Raw) Milk and Milk Products by Pregnant People and Children,” gives updated guidance highlighting emerging evidence that H5N1, or highly pathogenic avian influenza, may represent a new and potentially serious risk associated with raw milk. Research suggests the virus can be transmitted from infected dairy cattle into milk, where it can reach high concentrations and remain detectable in refrigerated raw milk for up to five weeks. “Nearly half of illnesses caused by raw dairy consumption occur in people under age 20 and a significant share of those cases are in children under five,” said Adam J. Ratner, MD, MPH, FAAP, lead author. “These illnesses can be severe and lead to life-threatening complications. Pasteurization, a safe, effective process of heating and cooling milk before consumption that has been used for more than a century, dramatically reduces the risks without taking away the nutritional value families rely on.” During the 2024 US dairy outbreak, infectious H5N1 virus was detected in nearly one-quarter of raw milk samples in affected areas, the AAP said meaning it “remains a credible, emerging threat.” Unpasteurized milk is already a well-documented source of serious pathogens including Listeria, E. coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter, and Brucella. These infections can lead to hospitalisation, life-threatening illness, miscarriage, and death, particularly in young children, pregnant people, and those with weakened immune systems. Those who are pregnant face especially high risks from foodborne infections, the AAP said. The incidence of listeriosis, for example, is estimated to be 12 to 14 times higher during pregnancy than in the general population. Infection can lead to miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery or severe illness in newborns. “Parents may choose raw milk because they have heard it is healthier or more natural, but the scientific evidence tells a different story,” said Mark R. Corkins, MD, FAAP, co-author of the policy statement. “Pasteurized dairy products provide the same essential nutrients without exposing children and families to preventable infections from dangerous bacteria and viruses. For infants, children and pregnant people, pasteurized dairy products are clearly the safest choice.” This policy statement updates guidance last provided in 2014 and reaffirmed in 2025. At the end of 2024 a new federal order in the US Department of Agriculture ordered mandatory testing of raw milk to bolster surveillance of H5N1. Only last week Sierra Nevada Cheese Company of Willows, California, voluntarily recalled all of its Graziers Raw Milk Cheese currently in the market because due to potential contamination with E-Coli. (OTCQX: VXRT) announced the publication of preclinical study results for its oral H5N1 vaccine candidate, VXA-H5-02, in the peer-reviewed journal Frontiers in Immunology. The study, conducted in ferrets, showed 100% survival following exposure to a lethal dose of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b virus. All unvaccinated control animals died by day six post-challenge, while all ferrets immunized with VXA-H5-02 survived. The vaccine also produced approximately a 2.3-log reduction in infectious viral shedding by day three post-challenge compared to controls. By days six to seven, viable virus fell below the limit of detection in nasal wash samples, and seven of eight animals cleared viral RNA by days eight to nine. The study found that VXA-H5-02 elicited both mucosal and systemic neutralizing antibody responses. Higher pre-challenge nasal IgA levels showed the strongest negative correlation with post-challenge viral shedding. Serum from vaccinated animals also demonstrated cross-neutralizing activity against divergent H5 strains, including H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1e. A clade-mismatched first-generation vaccine, encoding clade 2.1.3.2, conferred 37% survival against the clade 2.3.4.4b challenge, according to the study data. The vaccine was delivered via non-replicating recombinant adenovirus type 5 vectors expressing viral hemagglutinin. Because ferrets cannot use tablets, a liquid formulation was administered directly to the small intestine via endoscopic delivery on days zero and 28 to simulate enteric-coated tablet release. Challenge occurred on day 56. "The 100% survival rate following challenge with a lethal dose of virus underscores the robust immune protection our oral influenza vaccine candidates may be able to provide," said Dr. Sean Tucker, chief scientific officer of Vaxart. VXA-H5-02 has not been evaluated in humans and is not the subject of an investigational new drug application. Serious News for Serious Traders! Try StreetInsider.com Premium Free! supplementary_news.content: News World H5N1 detected in Australian sea lions in Australia — Mongabay UA.NEWS 07 October 2026 20:13 In Australia, the highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza strain has spread among wild birds and crossed over to mammals, including critically endangered Australian sea lions. The virus was detected on the country's mainland in August, and as of October 6, it had caused the deaths of thousands of birds in approximately 690 recorded incidents, Mongabay reports . One such incident may involve the confirmed infection or death of one or many animals. Infection in mammals In late August, H5N1 was confirmed in a long-nosed fur seal, the first recorded case of mammal infection on mainland Australia. A common dolphin found dead on the Fleurieu Peninsula in South Australia also tested positive. The virus was detected in two red foxes in the two urban areas of Adelaide and Torquay. According to Boston University's BEACON program, nearly simultaneous cases in foxes and a dolphin in South Australia showed that the virus had crossed between birds and mammals. In mid-September, an Australian sea lion died from H5N1 at Seal Bay on Kangaroo Island, home to the species' third-largest colony. On September 21, positive test results were obtained from three dead adult sea lions and a pup on North Page and South Page islands near South Australia. Between 10,000 and 12,000 Australian sea lions remain worldwide. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Monitoring and vaccination Scientists believe the virus likely spread to Australia from the Southern Ocean with seabirds, including giant petrels and skuas. According to Cornell University researcher Amandine Gamble, genetic data indicate that H5N1 did not arrive with migratory waterbirds that travel annually between Asia and Australia. Among the response measures, authorities and specialists are using disease monitoring and the removal of dead animal carcasses. In August, the government of New South Wales began vaccination trials for vulnerable captive birds, and on September 18 it began vaccinating little penguins in the wild. According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, at the time of publication, H5N1 had been detected in about 613 bird species and 112 mammal species worldwide. Losses in South America Previously, H5N1 caused significant losses among pinniped populations in South America. In Argentina, more than 95% of southern elephant seal pups born that winter died — about 17,400 out of approximately 18,000. A genetic study published in Nature Communications in November 2024 indicated direct H5N1 transmission between elephant seals — the first documented case of transmission of the virus between mammals. supplementary_news.content: Hausa Edition Podcast Conferences LeVogue Magazine Business News Print Advert Rates Online Advert Rates Contact Us Thursday, October 8, 2026 No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result 62 Officers Equipped For Avian Infuenza Control In Nasarawa Wildlife, Wetlands by Ahmed Tahir Ajobe 2 days ago in News Share on WhatsAppShare on FacebookShare on XTelegram The federal government has flagged off a six-day training for 62 multisectoral officers on surveillance of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in wildlife and wetlands. The training, holding in Akwanga, Nasarawa State, was opened by the chief veterinary officer of Nigeria, Dr Samuel Anzaku. Anzaku, who was represented by the national programme coordinator, Avian Influenza Control Programme, Dr Alao Mitchell, said the exercise was organised by the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Environment and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), with support from the Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection Systems (STRIDES) Project. With the theme, “Strengthening Wildlife Disease Surveillance for Early Detection of HPAI,” the training is aimed at building a skilled workforce tof detect and contain avian influenza at its source. Anzaku said HPAI remains a major threat to Nigeria’s poultry industry, food security, biodiversity and public health, noting that wild birds and wetlands are critical in the ecology and transmission of avian influenza viruses. He said the training was designed to enhance the capacity of officers to detect, report and respond to HPAI threats at the wildlife-livestock-human interface. According to him, effective surveillance requires more than sample collection. “It requires early recognition of unusual illness or mortality, accurate documentation, timely reporting, appropriate investigation, safe sample collection and laboratory confirmation, followed by prompt information-sharing and coordinated response,” he said. The CVO said the initiative aligns with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises food security, economic growth and livelihood protection, and the Nigeria Livestock Growth Acceleration Strategy (NLGAS), which depends on a strong animal health system. He stressed that tackling HPAI demands a One Health approach, bringing together veterinary services, wildlife and environmental authorities, public health institutions, laboratories, research bodies, local authorities and wetland communities. He urged participants drawn from Adamawa, Kano and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to leverage the training to clarify institutional roles, strengthen information sharing and build professional networks that will outlive the programme. He reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to improving animal disease surveillance, preparedness, laboratory capacity and rapid response in partnership with state governments, development partners and research institutions. supplementary_news.content_title: 高致病性禽流感A(H5)病毒2.3.2.1c和2.3.4.4分支持续进化导致的血凝素(HA)基因分支命名更新 - 生物通
supplementary_news.content: 高致病性禽流感A(H5)病毒2.3.2.1c和2.3.4.4分支持续进化导致的血凝素(HA)基因分支命名更新 《Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses》:Nomenclature Updates to the Hemagglutinin Gene Clade Designations Resulting From the Continued Evolution of High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza A(H5) Virus Clades 2.3.2.1c and 2.3.4.4 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月09日 来源:Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses 3.9 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access 背景与方法:研究人员通过系统发育和平均成对距离(average pairwise distance)方法,分析高致病性禽流感(HPAI)病毒(A/goose/Guangdong/96 lineage)A(H5)血凝素(HA)基因的进化分歧,以识别值得进行命名更新的分支(clade)。 结果与结论:基于该评估,建议了12个新分支命名,其依据是对2.3.2.1c和2.3.4.4分支病毒的划分;这些病毒自最近一次WHO/WOAH/FAO H5 Evolution Working Group更新以来,在非洲、南极、亚洲、欧洲、中东、美洲和大洋洲报告。 研究背景 下载细胞分析应用简报《利用安捷伦Seahorse实时细胞能量代谢分析评估 T 细胞的生物能量代谢平衡和备用呼吸能力》 领 取 研究人员开展的研究与主要结论 研究人员分析了自2014年底上次命名更新以来可获得的gs/GD/96 lineage A(H5) HA序列数据(2015年1月1日至2024年7月4日存入数据库),并根据WHO/WOAH/FAO H5 Evolution Working Group提出的命名,建议12个新分支命名。结论是2.3.2.1c和2.3.4.4需要拆分,形成2.3.2.1d–g和2.3.4.4a–h等新分支,以反映其在非洲、南极、亚洲、欧洲、中东、美洲和大洋洲的持续进化与地理扩散。该更新有利于A(H5)分支分类、候选疫苗病毒开发建议以及国际统一。 关键技术方法 研究人员使用截至2024年7月4日GISAID和GenBank的18,191条A(H5) HA序列。序列经定制Perl脚本和数据库过滤,去除重组迹象、重复、超过5个模糊核苷酸、少于60%比对长度或移码的序列。经MAFFT v7.388比对,并用BioEdit 7.2.5修剪至成熟A(H5) HA蛋白基因序列起始。采用FastTree v2.1.11构建近似最大似然树(GTR+GAMMA,10,000重采样用于局部拓扑支持),用LABEL H5v2015分类模块自动注释。MEGA5.1计算成对p距离矩阵,定制Perl脚本计算组平均值。新分支命名标准为:存在2015年后采样病毒、形成局部支持值≥60%的单系簇、分支内平均成对距离≤1.5%,但系统发育和监测数据不足支持拆分时放宽该上限。第五级组在第四级分支右侧加字母。 研究结果 3 Results:遗传分歧与分支拆分依据。通过重建系统发育,研究发现大多数循环分支为单系群。对含新序列的现有分支分析分支内平均成对距离后,依据既定命名标准,研究人员判断2.3.2.1c和2.3.4.4需要拆分。2.3.2.1c内部APD为3.93%,病毒自2015年以来在印度尼西亚、印度、西非、中国和越南循环;其被分为新亚分支2.3.2.1d至2.3.2.1g,平均分支内APD为2.04%。中国和越南2012—2017年病毒仍归2.3.2.1c;2014—2016年分化形成2.3.2.1d;越南及后来柬埔寨2020—2024年病毒归2.3.2.1e;2013—2017年扩散至印度、中东和非洲的病毒归2.3.2.1f;印度尼西亚2012—2016年病毒归2.3.2.1g,反映其单系性和局部循环。 新分支描述/候选疫苗病毒(CVVs)。研究给出新分支描述和WHO候选疫苗病毒(CVV,candidate vaccine virus)。例如2.3.2.1c对应中国、日本2009—2019年,之前CVV为A/duck/Vietnam/NCVD-1584/2012;2.3.2.1d为中国2014—2016年,CVV为A/chicken/Guiyang/1153/2016;2.3.2.1e为越南、柬埔寨、老挝2012—2024年,CVV包括A/duck/Vietnam/NCVD-1584/2012和A/Cambodia/SVH240441/2024;2.3.2.1f为中国、印度、中东、非洲2013—2018年,CVV为A/chicken/Ghana/20/2015;2.3.2.1g为印度尼西亚2012—2023年,无CVV。 2.3.4.4的进一步划分、2.3.4.4-like与未更新分支。2.3.4.4自2.3.4内其他第四级群分化以来表现出3.50%的高APD,反映高度分歧A(H5) HA基因的快速出现、进化、宿主范围扩张和地理扩张。2.3.4.4包含N1、N2、N3、N5、N6、N7和N8等多种NA亚型,形成多个单系谱系,被分为2.3.4.4a至2.3.4.4h。2.3.4.4a为2013—2015年中国和2015—2017年越南的A(H5N6);2.3.4.4b含N1—N8,从东亚扩散至非洲、美洲、南极和欧洲,并传播至多种哺乳动物,成为全球优势分支,造成野生和家养哺乳动物检测、欧洲毛皮养殖水貂和狐狸、美国奶牛、南美和南极海洋哺乳动物、欧洲/北美/亚洲猫的暴发,以及暴露后散发人感染;2.3.4.4c为A(H5N2)和A(H5N8),经候鸟从东亚引入欧洲、台湾、日本和北美;2.3.4.4d为2015—2016年仅中国的A(H5N6);2.3.4.4e、2.3.4.4g和2.3.4.4h为2013—2020年东亚和东南亚循环病毒。除2.3.4.4c和2.3.4.4f外,多数2.3.4.4亚分支均报告人感染,且每个亚分支已开发WHO大流行前候选疫苗病毒。2.3.4.4b分支内APD为1.98%,代表超过13,000条序列,超过1.5%阈值;但由于特定暴发序列过度代表和近期引入地区数据不足,进一步细分被推迟。2.3.4.4a–h划分排除了125个位于系统发育基部、不符合亚分支的病毒,暂命名为“2.3.4.4-like”。其他分支如2.1.3.2a也出现持续遗传分歧且部分超过1.5%阈值,但因近年有限循环和持续循环不确定性未进一步细分;认为“灭绝”的分支因无新序列未更新。 A(H5)病毒以及哺乳动物和散发人感染进行全球监测、监测和表征,对评估这些新分支的流行率和公共卫生意义至关重要。作者Tommy T. A(H5N1)广泛洲际传播外,A(H5N2)、A(H5N6)和A(H5N8)也全球传播。广泛地理扩散凸显其动态进化,近期研究强调其跨时间和地理区域、野鸟与家禽之间以及向哺乳动物(包括美国奶牛)溢出的遗传分歧。新遗传群出现与持续人感染报告重合:2.3.2.1c supplementary_news.content: 🧐正在智能总结中... 南海大沥 行花街,买年货 防护同样好紧要 在新春到来之际 人员流动和聚集将会明显增加 各类病毒传播风险随之增大 沥仔提醒你 这7种病毒 最近要特别提防! 新冠病毒感染 目前广东省新型冠状病毒感染疫情处于社区流行第一波高峰后的回落阶段。 春节人员流动大,加之近期入境人员防疫政策调整,部分地区疫情可能有所波动,但出现大幅度反弹的可能性不大。 重点防控场所:医院、福利机构、养老机构、大型企业、学校、学前教育机构等,重点防控地区为农村地区。 防病指引 1. 做防护:日常要坚持做好勤洗手、戴口罩、勤通风、一米线这“防疫四件套”。 2. 打疫苗:建议在没有接种禁忌症的情况下,符合条件者尽早接种新冠病毒疫苗。60岁以上人群、严重慢性病患者、免疫功能低下人员优先推荐接种新冠病毒疫苗。 已完成全程接种的18-59岁人群按照6个月的时间间隔尽快接种加强针;60岁以上老年人按照3个月以上的时间间隔尽快接种加强针。 3. 早排查:每天进行自我健康监测,如有出现发热、干咳、乏力、咽痛、嗅(味)觉减退、腹泻等不适症状时,避免带病上学或上班,视情况及时到附近医院发热门诊就诊;就医途中全程佩戴口罩,尽量避免乘坐公共交通工具。 诺如病毒感染 广东每年9月至次年3月为诺如病毒感染暴发高峰期,以接触传播和食源性传播为主。 1月发生诺如病毒感染暴发疫情的风险较高,重点防控场所为学校和托幼机构等集体单位。 防病指引 01 校园防病要点 学生健康管理:做好学生个人健康管理、严格落实晨午检、因病缺勤查因等工作。 厨工健康管理:加强对厨工的健康管理,制作食物和配餐过程中要佩戴口罩和做好手卫生,有消化道症状要暂时调离岗位。 饮用水管理:做好饮用水的管理,定期清洗、消毒滤网和二次供水设施,做好饮用水管道维护,师生饮用水烧开后饮用。 环境清洁消毒:开窗通风和环境(门把手、扶手、电梯按钮、马桶按钮等)高频接触部位清洁消毒。 病例管理:一旦出现呕吐、腹泻症状的病人,要立即就医并隔离,做好呕吐物处理,做好清洁消毒;病例持续增多应立即向主管部门和属地疾控机构报告。 02 家庭防病要点 家长和儿童注意个人卫生,养成勤洗手、不喝生水、生熟食物分开、食物煮熟煮透等健康生活习惯。 人感染禽流感 2022年以来,全国仍陆续有人感染H5N6、H9N2等散发病例报告。 冬春季为人感染禽流感疫情易发季节,广东发生H5N6、H9N2等人感染禽流感散发病例的风险较高。 重点防控场所:活禽经营非限制区以及未全面落实活禽经营卫生管理措施的区域。 防病指引 ✔要洗手:尤其是接触禽鸟后及饭前便后。 ✔要煮熟:禽肉和蛋要煮熟后再吃。 ✔要就医:出现发热、咳嗽等呼吸道症状,避免带病上学或上班,视情况及时就近就医。有接触过禽鸟要记得告诉医生。 ✘不要食用病、死禽肉。 ✘不要购买来源不明的禽鸟类产品,也不要光顾活禽售卖流动摊档。 ✘不要在活禽档口食宿。 流 感 近期广东省流感样病例就诊比例迅速上升后有所回落(考虑受新冠病毒感染影响),流感病毒检出率低,处于较低水平。 重点防控场所:各类学校、托幼机构、医院、福利机构、养老机构、公安司法监管场所、工厂企业、物流园等集体单位。 防病指引 1. 打疫苗:根据《中国流感疫苗预防接种技术指南(2022-2023)》,重点和高风险人群建议优先接种流感疫苗。 2. 保持良好卫生习惯:坚持勤洗手、戴口罩、常通风等卫生习惯。 勤洗手:用肥皂/洗手液及流动水洗手。 戴口罩:特别是在人多的公共场所,避免接触有流感样症状的患者(体温≥38°C,有咳嗽或咽喉疼痛)。 勤通风:定期开窗通风,做好通风与环境消毒等工作。 3. 早就医:出现流感样症状(体温≥38°C,有咳嗽或咽喉疼痛)时戴口罩,避免带病上学或上班,视情况及时就近就医,避免带病上学或上班。 布鲁氏菌病 近年来因饮用未经消毒的生鲜羊奶在局部地区(如粤东、粤北地区)引起布鲁氏菌病聚集性疫情时有发生。时值春节来临,进入羊肉和奶制品加工处理和消费等危险因素暴露高峰期,市民应提高警惕。 防病指引 1. 不饮生奶:尽量买正规厂家生产的合格奶及其奶制品。如确实购买了私营农场或个人贩卖的生的牛、羊奶,也必须“煮三沸”,约3-5分钟(由于牛羊奶比较粘稠,沸点低,加热时要等冒泡离开火源,等泡沫下去后再加热,如此重复三次)才能饮用,隔水蒸也不行!!! 2. 煮熟煮透:把肉做熟了吃,特别是不要为了追求鲜嫩,吃没涮熟、烤熟的牛羊肉。 3. 戴手套:皮肤有破损时戴手套处理生肉及内脏。 4. 个人防护:如果是畜牧业等职业人群,除了做好以上措施,还要注意个人防护。 猴 痘 当前全球猴痘疫情波及范围广,美洲和欧洲两个高风险区域的猴痘疫情仍未得到有效控制;我国境内及港澳台地区相继发现输入性个案,广东发生猴痘输入性疫情的风险仍将持续存在。 防病指引 一般居民不必过度紧张,保持良好的卫生习惯,尽量避免接触野生动物。 食源性疾病 目前广东正处于秋冬季,为细菌性食源性疾病暴发的低发期,但该季节也是诺如等病毒感染暴发的高峰期,需要警惕诺如病毒通过食源性途径引起感染暴发可能性。 近年,广东毒蘑菇及有毒植物中毒风险较高,全年各月均有发生。1月份,气温逐渐下降,不利于细菌繁殖,细菌性食源性疾病将有所减少。 防病指引 1. 遵守食品安全要点:生熟食物分开处理和存放;食物要煮熟煮透方可食用;尽可能当餐烹调当餐食用,如有吃剩的食物,应放入冰箱,食前彻底加热。 2. 厨工健康管理:学校加强对厨工的健康管理,制作食物和配餐过程中要佩戴口罩和做好手卫生,有消化道症状要暂时调离岗位。 3. 加强知识宣传:学校加强对学生的宣传,不得随意或“凭经验”采摘和食用野生果实。 沥仔要再次提醒大家 注意日常卫生习惯 防止病从口入哦 最新经济发展、就业招聘 疫苗接种资讯 请点击关注 “南海大沥”官方微信公众号 关注"南海大沥"视频号 了解大沥更多资讯 来源:南方日报、广东疾控、健康南海 编辑:彭雪媚 校对:曾梦怡、吕燕珊、霍嘉仪 监制:何锦婷、张秋枫 0 10万+ 好物推荐 【优惠秒杀】高州柠檬桂圆肉-250克/罐 ¥ 40¥ 45 去购买 【优惠秒杀】花茶 ¥ 24¥ 30 去购买 【佛山石榜系列】贞观禅心茶具套装 ¥ 1380 去购买 【优惠秒杀】高州柠檬桂圆肉-250克/罐 ¥ 40¥ 45 去购买 更多好物 热门评论 抢先发表观点更易上热评哦~ 相关新闻 钟南山最新提醒:呼吸道合胞病毒暂无特效药,最好的预防办法就是注射抗体 09-20 这种病毒升至中流行水平! 官方动物疾病序列常因报告延迟而不完整。这项回顾性观察研究评估了增加模型复杂度是否会增强对最终官方报告暴发当量计数的概率临近预报。研究人员从世界动物卫生组织(WOAH)世界动物卫生信息系统(WAHIS)的固定提取中重建历史信息状态,其中包括46,860起高致病性禽流感(HPAI)和72,690起非洲猪瘟(ASF)暴发。研究人员使用加权区间评分(WIS)、校准诊断、分块自助法、模拟以及单独冻结的美国农业部动植物卫生检验局(USDA APHIS)迁移评估,在2024–2025年的78个锁定截点上评估了12种预指定方法。主要HPAI分析包括来自115个国家–宿主单元的35,880个观测。在周关闭时,仅7.6%的最终HPAI和6.7%的最终ASF暴发当量可见,完整性随宿主、地区、年份、季节和工作量变化。预指定的主要假设未获支持:延迟感知时间网络比分层贝叶斯比较器差6.9%,关系图仅使WIS改变0.4%。梯度提升分位数回归使WIS改善18.5%(绝对差?0.0397,95%区间?0.0553至?0.0255),但在高报告量单位中改善达26.0%,并在报告史极少的单位中逆转为6.3%劣势。在队列年龄0时,以部分计数为条件比匹配的无延迟网络差24.7%,此后表现更好。报告较慢的ASF系统逆转了汇总对比,而APHIS模块在系统特异性重新训练后使WIS改善10.1%。添加显式零处质量使透明比较器改善18.8%,并导致与梯度提升无可检测差异;在相同重校准下神经模型仍差17.4%。在探索性分析中,梯度提升在所有六种队列定义和所有三种成熟期限下均越过预指定5%门槛。对于排除训练的高报告量国家和地区,性能显著恶化。这些估计针对所研究监测条件下最终官方报告的暴发当量,而非未检测感染。
